claim: A BLAST search revealed significant (E = 5 × 10−4) similarity between a small region (amino acids 388–420) of human Repo-Man and Ki-67.
source: A BLAST search revealed significant (E = 5 × 10−4) similarity between a small region (amino acids 388–420) of human Repo-Man and Ki-67 (Figure 1A1,2), a very large protein that exhibits strong links to cell proliferation (Gerdes et al., 1983).
evidence: The claim is supported by computational analysis (BLAST search) with a specific E-value, and references a figure showing the similarity.

claim: The region conserved between Repo-Man and Ki-67 contains the PP1 binding motif (RVTF) of Repo-Man, which is conserved as RVSF in human Ki-67.
source: The region conserved between Repo-Man and Ki-67 contains the PP1 binding motif (RVTF) of Repo-Man, which is conserved as RVSF in human Ki-67 (Figure 1C3).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1C3.

claim: Ki-67 is a PP1-interacting protein (PIP) in vivo.
source: To analyse if Ki-67 was a cell-cycle regulated PIP in vivo, we performed a tethering/recruitment experiment (Vagnarelli et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from tethering/recruitment experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Ki-67 wild type construct recruited PP1 to the LacO integration site.
source: Furthermore, the Ki-67 wt construct recruited PP1 to the same spot (Figure 1C2″).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1C2″.

claim: Ki-67 recruitment of PP1 is more efficient in interphase than in mitosis.
source: Quantification of the PP1 signal intensity at the GFP:Lac repressor spot compared to the general nuclear distribution (excluding nucleoli) revealed that Ki-67 recruitment of PP1 is more efficient in interphase than in mitosis and that PP1γ is recruited more efficiently than PP1β during interphase (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of PP1 signal intensity shown in Figure 1D.

claim: PP1γ is recruited more efficiently than PP1β during interphase by Ki-67.
source: Quantification of the PP1 signal intensity at the GFP:Lac repressor spot compared to the general nuclear distribution (excluding nucleoli) revealed that Ki-67 recruitment of PP1 is more efficient in interphase than in mitosis and that PP1γ is recruited more efficiently than PP1β during interphase (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of PP1 signal intensity shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ki-67 depletion has no effect on the accumulation of RFP:PP1γ in the nucleolus.
source: Ki-67 depletion in a HeLa cell line has no effect on the accumulation of RFP:PP1γ in the nucleolus (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2[1,4]).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: RRP1B is the targeting subunit for PP1 nucleolar localisation.
source: Indeed, the targeting subunit for PP1 nucleolar localisation has been recently reported to be RRP1B (Chamousset et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: PP1γ localised normally on the spindle and at kinetochores in both control and Ki-67 depleted cells in early mitosis.
source: In early mitosis, PP1γ localised normally on the spindle and at kinetochores in both control and Ki-67 depleted cells (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2[2,5]).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: A significant decrease in PP1 levels on anaphase chromatin was observed in Ki-67 depleted cells.
source: However, we observed a significant decrease in PP1 levels on anaphase chromatin in Ki-67 depleted cells (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2[3′,6′]).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Repo-Man and Sds22 are responsible for targeting PP1 to anaphase chromatin.
source: Previous reports identified Repo-Man and Sds22 as responsible for targeting PP1 to anaphase chromatin (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006; Wurzenberger et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ki-67 is one of the several factors contributing to the accumulation of PP1γ on chromatin during mitotic exit.
source: Thus, Ki-67 is one of the several factors contributing to the accumulation of PP1γ on chromatin during mitotic exit.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing decreased PP1 levels on anaphase chromatin in Ki-67 depleted cells.

claim: B23 is phosphorylated both in interphase and in mitosis by several kinases.
source: B23 is phosphorylated both in interphase and in mitosis by several kinases (Pfaff and Anderer, 1988; Jiang et al., 2000; Louvet et al., 2006; Krause and Hoffmann, 2010; Ramos-Echazabal et al., 2012; Reboutier et al., 2012), including CyclinB/CDK1 at T199 (Tokuyama et al., 2001) in mitosis and by casein kinase II (CKII) on S125 during interphase (Szebeni et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: CyclinB/CDK1 phosphorylates B23 at T199 in mitosis.
source: B23 is phosphorylated both in interphase and in mitosis by several kinases (Pfaff and Anderer, 1988; Jiang et al., 2000; Louvet et al., 2006; Krause and Hoffmann, 2010; Ramos-Echazabal et al., 2012; Reboutier et al., 2012), including CyclinB/CDK1 at T199 (Tokuyama et al., 2001) in mitosis and by casein kinase II (CKII) on S125 during interphase (Szebeni et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Casein kinase II (CKII) phosphorylates B23 on S125 during interphase.
source: B23 is phosphorylated both in interphase and in mitosis by several kinases (Pfaff and Anderer, 1988; Jiang et al., 2000; Louvet et al., 2006; Krause and Hoffmann, 2010; Ramos-Echazabal et al., 2012; Reboutier et al., 2012), including CyclinB/CDK1 at T199 (Tokuyama et al., 2001) in mitosis and by casein kinase II (CKII) on S125 during interphase (Szebeni et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The levels of B23 S125 phosphorylation were significantly increased following Ki-67 depletion in exponential cultures and in prometaphase cells.
source: Use of phospho-specific antibodies revealed a reproducible difference in nucleophosmin/B23 phosphorylation on S125 in the presence and absence of Ki-67 exponential cultures and in prometaphase cells (Figure 1F). In both cases, the levels of S125ph were significantly increased following Ki-67 depletion.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: No significant difference in the phosphorylation status of B23 at T199 was observed in the presence or absence of Ki-67.
source: In contrast, we observed no significant difference in the phosphorylation status of B23 at T199 in the presence or absence of Ki-67 (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data that is mentioned but not shown.

claim: Ki-67 is a functional PP1-targeting subunit in vivo.
source: These experiments support the notion that Ki-67 is a functional PP1-targeting subunit in vivo.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the B23 phosphorylation data.

claim: Ki-67 is one of many nucleolar proteins that are recruited to the chromosome periphery at the transition from prophase to prometaphase.
source: Ki-67 is one of many nucleolar proteins that are recruited to the chromosome periphery at the transition from prophase to prometaphase.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Ki-67 localization.

claim: Nucleolin failed to accumulate at the chromosome periphery in the absence of Ki-67.
source: We first examined the localisation of the endogenous nucleolin using a specific antibody. Indeed, nucleolin failed to accumulate at the chromosome periphery in the absence of Ki-67 (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The nucleolin mislocalization phenotype was observed using all of the siRNAs tested against Ki-67.
source: The phenotype was observed using all of the siRNAs that we have tested and was rescued by an siRNA-resistant cDNA (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplements 1, 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from multiple siRNAs shown in Figure 2B and supplementary figures.

claim: The nucleolin mislocalization phenotype was rescued by an siRNA-resistant cDNA.
source: The phenotype was observed using all of the siRNAs that we have tested and was rescued by an siRNA-resistant cDNA (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplements 1, 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 2B and supplementary figures.

claim: In the absence of Ki-67, NIFK failed to properly accumulate around the mitotic chromosomes in early mitosis.
source: The nucleolar localisation of GFP-NIFK in interphase was unaltered after Ki-67 depletion (Figure 2C8), but in early mitosis the protein failed to properly accumulate around the mitotic chromosomes (Figure 2C5–7).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In metaphase cells depleted of Ki-67, NIFK accumulated in large cytoplasmic aggregates, one of which was frequently found to 'cap' one end of the cluster of chromosomes on the metaphase plate.
source: Instead, in metaphase cells, it accumulated in large cytoplasmic aggregates, one of which was frequently found to 'cap' one end of the cluster of chromosomes on the metaphase plate (Figure 2C5).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2C5.

claim: During mitotic exit in the absence of Ki-67, GFP-NIFK accumulated in NDF-like cytoplasmic aggregates that persisted until the reformation of the nuclear membrane.
source: During mitotic exit, in the absence of Ki-67, GFP-NIFK accumulated in NDF-like cytoplasmic aggregates that persisted until the reformation of the nuclear membrane (Figure 2C5–7).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: All four novel cPERPs tested were mislocalised in Ki-67-depleted cells.
source: Remarkably, all were mislocalised in Ki-67-depleted cells, and all were frequently observed to 'cap' one end of the metaphase plate (Figure 2D3,7,11,15).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: All four novel cPERPs tested were frequently observed to 'cap' one end of the metaphase plate in Ki-67-depleted cells.
source: Remarkably, all were mislocalised in Ki-67-depleted cells, and all were frequently observed to 'cap' one end of the metaphase plate (Figure 2D3,7,11,15).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The GFP-containing aggregates observed in mitosis in Ki-67-depleted cells did not correspond to nucleolar remnants or any other recognisable electron-dense structures such as NDFs.
source: Correlative light-microscopy/Electron microscopy (CLEM) analysis of cells transfected with both GFP-cPERP-C and the indicated siRNA oligos eliminated this hypothesis. The GFP-containing aggregates observed in mitosis in Ki-67-depleted cells did not correspond to nucleolar remnants or any other recognisable electron-dense structures such as NDFs (Dundr et al., 2000; Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by CLEM data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is a 'fuzzy' transition zone between the electron-dense chromatin and the cytoplasm in control cells.
source: Examination of electron micrographs of control and Ki-67-depleted cells at higher magnification revealed a subtle difference in the appearance of the edge of the chromosomes. In control cells there was a 'fuzzy' transition zone between the electron-dense chromatin and the cytoplasm (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The transition between chromatin and cytoplasm appeared to be more abrupt in Ki-67-depleted chromosomes.
source: This transition appeared to be more abrupt in Ki-67-depleted chromosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data.

claim: There is normally a gradual decrease in density at the edge of mitotic chromosomes.
source: This was confirmed by line scans across the chromosome-to-cytoplasm boundary, which showed that there is normally a gradual decrease in density at the edge of mitotic chromosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by line scan analysis of electron microscopy data.

claim: The density transition at the edge of mitotic chromosomes was significantly more abrupt in the absence of Ki-67.
source: This was confirmed by line scans across the chromosome-to-cytoplasm boundary, which showed that there is normally a gradual decrease in density at the edge of mitotic chromosomes. This transition was significantly more abrupt in the absence of Ki-67 (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by line scan analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Depletion of cPERP-B, -D, or -E using RNAi failed to alter the striking perichromosomal localization of Ki-67.
source: However, depletion of cPERP-B, -D, or -E using RNAi (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) failed to alter the striking perichromosomal localization of Ki-67 (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ki-67 is upstream of the other components in the assembly of the perichromosomal compartment.
source: This is consistent with Ki-67 being upstream of the other components in the assembly of the perichromosomal compartment.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that depletion of other cPERPs does not affect Ki-67 localization.

claim: Both mRFP:Ki-67-wt and mRFP:Ki-67-RASA proteins rescued the localisation of endogenous nucleolin throughout mitosis in cells transfected with Ki-67 siRNAs.
source: Both mRFP:Ki-67-wt and mRFP:Ki-67-RASA proteins rescued the localisation of endogenous nucleolin throughout mitosis in cells transfected with Ki-67 siRNAs. In transfected cells, nucleolin was once again concentrated at the chromosome periphery from prometaphase through telophase (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ki-67 acts as a scaffold for formation of the perichromosomal compartment.
source: When combined with our previous observations these data support the hypothesis that Ki-67 acts as a scaffold for formation of the perichromosomal compartment.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the rescue experiments showing that PP1-binding is not required for Ki-67 function in perichromosomal compartment assembly.

claim: The chromosome periphery phenotypes observed following Ki-67 depletion by siRNA-5 are not due to off-target effects.
source: Importantly, this rescue experiment also confirmed that the chromosome periphery phenotypes observed following Ki-67 depletion by siRNA-5 are not due to off-target effects.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the rescue experiment results.

claim: Levels of intrinsic DNA damage are low in mitotic cells under the culture conditions used.
source: Immunostaining for 53BP1, a protein that associates with DNA damage foci revealed that levels of intrinsic DNA damage are low in mitotic cells under our culture conditions (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: DNA damage levels were not substantially increased in chromosomes lacking Ki-67.
source: These levels were not substantially increased in chromosomes lacking Ki-67.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data for DNA damage markers.

claim: Neither the localisation nor abundance of KIF4A was altered in the absence of Ki-67.
source: The converse is not true, however, as neither the localisation nor abundance (as determined by immunostaining) of KIF4A was altered in the absence of Ki-67 (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Ki-67 depletion does not affect the known mitotic chromosome structural proteins.
source: Thus, Ki-67 depletion does not affect the known mitotic chromosome structural proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the KIF4A localization data.

claim: Chromosomes depleted of Ki-67 efficiently regain their normal morphology after two rounds of unfolding and refolding in the IMS assay.
source: This experiment showed clearly that chromosomes depleted of Ki-67 efficiently regain their normal morphology after two rounds of unfolding and refolding. Thus, the perichromosomal layer is not required for maintenance of the intrinsic structure of mitotic chromosomes (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by IMS assay data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: The perichromosomal layer is not required for maintenance of the intrinsic structure of mitotic chromosomes.
source: This experiment showed clearly that chromosomes depleted of Ki-67 efficiently regain their normal morphology after two rounds of unfolding and refolding. Thus, the perichromosomal layer is not required for maintenance of the intrinsic structure of mitotic chromosomes (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the IMS assay results.

claim: In Ki-67-depleted cells, B23 was never observed to associate with the chromosomes during mitosis.
source: In Ki-67-depleted cells, B23 was never observed to associate with the chromosomes during mitosis. Instead, it started forming cytoplasmic aggregates just after anaphase onset (Figure 6A, 45').
evidence: The claim is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In control cells there was a relatively even distribution of chromatin-associated nucleolin between daughter cells.
source: While in control cells there was a relatively even distribution of chromatin-associated nucleolin between daughter cells, in Ki-67-depleted cells the nucleolin aggregates were often not chromatin bound and their distribution between daughter cells tended to be more asymmetric (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: In Ki-67-depleted cells the nucleolin aggregates were often not chromatin bound and their distribution between daughter cells tended to be more asymmetric.
source: While in control cells there was a relatively even distribution of chromatin-associated nucleolin between daughter cells, in Ki-67-depleted cells the nucleolin aggregates were often not chromatin bound and their distribution between daughter cells tended to be more asymmetric (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The ultrastructure of the reformed nucleoli appeared to be normal following Ki-67 depletion, with fibrillar centres, dense fibrillar component, and granular component all readily observed.
source: Furthermore, the ultrastructure of the reformed nucleoli appeared to be normal, with fibrillar centres, dense fibrillar component, and granular component all readily observed (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ki-67 is apparently not required for the structural organisation within interphase nucleoli.
source: Thus, Ki-67 is apparently not required for the structural organisation within interphase nucleoli.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that nucleolar ultrastructure appears normal after Ki-67 depletion.

claim: In the HeLa cell line used, 3.5 ± 0.3 nucleoli per nucleus were observed.
source: In our line of HeLa cells, we observed 3.5 ± 0.3 nucleoli per nucleus (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative microscopy data shown in Figure 7D,E.

claim: Following Ki-67 depletion, the number of nucleoli observed dropped to 1.6 ± 0.3.
source: This changed dramatically following Ki-67 depletion, when the number of nucleoli observed dropped to 1.6 ± 0.3.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative microscopy data.

claim: Chromosomes lacking a perichromosomal layer might associate with one another more closely than normal, thus promoting NOR fusion during reactivation.
source: This strongly suggests that chromosomes lacking a perichromosomal layer might associate with one another more closely than normal, thus promoting NOR fusion during reactivation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation of reduced nucleolar number after Ki-67 depletion.

claim: Ki-67-depleted cells tended to be smaller and to have smaller nuclei.
source: Ki-67-depleted cells tended to be smaller and to have smaller nuclei (Figure 7A–C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative microscopy data shown in Figure 7A–C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The smaller cell and nuclear size in Ki-67-depleted cells was not due to an accumulation of the cells in G1.
source: This was not due to an accumulation of the cells in G1, as shown by FACs analysis (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), but could potentially be due to ribosomal insufficiency.
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ki-67-depleted nuclei tend to have a smaller aggregate nucleolar area.
source: First, if we calculate the total nucleolar area in optical sections of Ki-67-depleted nuclei, we find that these nuclei tend to have a smaller aggregate nucleolar area (Figure 7F,G, Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative microscopy data shown in Figure 7F,G and Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: Reactivation of ribosomal clusters following mitotic exit may be less efficient in Ki-67-depleted cells.
source: If we assume total nucleolar area to be a proxy for the number of genes involved in rDNA transcription, this suggests that reactivation of ribosomal clusters following mitotic exit may be less efficient in Ki-67-depleted cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation of smaller nucleolar area in Ki-67-depleted cells.

claim: Northern analysis revealed decreased levels of pre-rRNA species in Ki-67-depleted cells, consistent with lower levels of rRNA transcription.
source: This is consistent with the results of a Northern analysis of total rRNA in control and Ki-67-depleted cells, which revealed decreased levels of pre-rRNA species, consistent with lower levels of rRNA transcription in the depleted cells (Figure 7H).
evidence: The claim is supported by Northern blot data shown in Figure 7H.

claim: In HT1080 cells, the 13p locus tends to localise in the nuclear interior where it is usually closely associated with a nucleolus.
source: In this cell line the 13p locus (visualized as a GFP spot) tends to localise in the nuclear interior (Figure 8A1) where it is usually closely associated with a nucleolus (Figure 8B1).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8A1 and 8B1.

claim: Depletion of Ki-67 caused the tagged 13p locus to move from the nuclear interior towards the nuclear periphery.
source: Depletion of Ki-67 had a strong effect on the nuclear localization of chromosome 13p. In cells depleted of Ki-67, the tagged 13p locus tended to move from the nuclear interior towards the nuclear periphery (Figure 8A3).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8A3.

claim: The reorganization of chromosome 13p following Ki-67 depletion was correlated with a disengagement from the nucleolus.
source: This reorganization of chromosome 13p was correlated with a disengagement from the nucleolus (Figure 8B2,3).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8B2,3.

claim: The nuclear reorganization phenotypes following Ki-67 depletion are consistent with decreased activity of the ribosomal gene clusters and with altered interactions between chromosomes.
source: Thus, although Ki-67 depletion and loss of much or all of the perichromosomal compartment has little obvious effect on chromosome structure or segregation in the first mitosis after depletion, after mitotic exit the nucleus undergoes fundamental changes consistent with decreased activity of the ribosomal gene clusters and with altered interactions between chromosomes.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the chromosome positioning and nucleolar association data.

claim: The perichromosomal layer represents 1.4% of the chromosome proteome.
source: The perichromosomal layer represents 1.4% of the chromosome proteome (Ohta et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous proteomic study.

claim: Ki-67 is an antigen recognised by a monoclonal antibody generated by immunizing mice with nuclei of Hodgkin lymphoma cells.
source: Ki-67 is an antigen recognised by a monoclonal antibody generated by immunizing mice with nuclei of Hodgkin lymphoma cells (Gerdes et al., 1983).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to the original study describing Ki-67.

claim: Ki-67 is nuclear only in proliferating cells.
source: Because Ki-67 is nuclear only in proliferating cells, it is widely used as a marker to assess cell proliferation.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Ki-67.

claim: Immuno-histochemical assessment of the proportion of cells staining for nuclear Ki-67 is used to predict the responsiveness or resistance of tumours to therapy.
source: For example, immuno-histochemical assessment of the proportion of cells staining for nuclear Ki-67 is used to predict the responsiveness or resistance of tumours to therapy (Dowsett et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a clinical study.

claim: Ki-67 protein is predominantly localised in the cortex and dense fibrillar components of the nucleolus during interphase.
source: Ki-67 protein is predominantly localised in the cortex and dense fibrillar components of the nucleolus during interphase (Kill, 1996; MacCallum and Hall, 2000b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: During mitosis Ki-67 relocates to the periphery of the condensed chromosomes.
source: During mitosis it relocates to the periphery of the condensed chromosomes (Verheijen et al., 1989b; Isola et al., 1990).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Approximately 40% of the cellular pool of Ki-67 protein is present on isolated mitotic chromosomes.
source: Approximately 40% of the cellular pool of protein is present on isolated mitotic chromosomes (Ohta et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous proteomic study.

claim: Hyperphosphorylated Ki-67 does not bind DNA during mitosis.
source: Hyperphosphorylated Ki-67 does not bind DNA during mitosis (Endl and Gerdes, 2000; MacCallum and Hall, 1999) and is characterized by increased mobility, on mitotic chromosomes measured by FRAP.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In interphase, non-phosphorylated Ki-67 binds DNA and does not recover after FRAP.
source: In interphase, non-phosphorylated Ki-67 binds DNA and does not recover after FRAP (Saiwaki et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Ki-67 functions in mitosis in stabilisation and maintenance of the mitotic spindle by recruiting Hklp2 to mitotic chromosomes.
source: Recently, it was reported that Ki-67 also functions in mitosis in stabilisation and maintenance of the mitotic spindle by recruiting Hklp2 to mitotic chromosomes (Vanneste et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Ki-67 is ancestral to the PP1 targeting subunit Repo-Man.
source: In this study, we have identified Ki-67 as ancestral to the PP1 targeting subunit Repo-Man (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006) and have shown that Ki-67 is a PIP (PP1 Interacting Protein) that contributes to the phospho-regulation of nucleophosmin/B23 by CKII.
evidence: The claim is based on phylogenetic analysis and experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Ki-67 is a PIP (PP1 Interacting Protein) that contributes to the phospho-regulation of nucleophosmin/B23 by CKII.
source: In this study, we have identified Ki-67 as ancestral to the PP1 targeting subunit Repo-Man (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006) and have shown that Ki-67 is a PIP (PP1 Interacting Protein) that contributes to the phospho-regulation of nucleophosmin/B23 by CKII.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data on PP1 binding and B23 phosphorylation presented in the study.

claim: Ki-67 is a major organiser of the perichromosomal layer, possibly acting as an interaction platform.
source: Ki-67 is also a major organiser of the perichromosomal layer, possibly acting as an interaction platform.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing that multiple proteins fail to localize to the chromosome periphery when Ki-67 is depleted.

claim: Ki-67 depletion prevents all nucleolar proteins tested from accumulating around the chromosomes in mitosis.
source: Remarkably, Ki-67 depletion prevents all nucleolar proteins tested from accumulating around the chromosomes in mitosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing mislocalization of multiple nucleolar proteins after Ki-67 depletion.

claim: Chromosomes in cells depleted of Ki-67 appear to lack most or all of their perichromosomal layer.
source: Thus, chromosomes in cells depleted of Ki-67 appear to lack most or all of their perichromosomal layer.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing loss of multiple perichromosomal proteins and altered electron microscopy appearance.

claim: Loss of the perichromosomal layer does not detectibly compromise the condensed morphology or intrinsic structure of mitotic chromosomes.
source: Interestingly, loss of the perichromosomal layer does not detectibly compromise the condensed morphology or intrinsic structure of mitotic chromosomes but does result in significant changes in nucleolar morphology and nuclear organization in the following interphase.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from chromosome spreads and IMS assays.

claim: Loss of the perichromosomal layer results in significant changes in nucleolar morphology and nuclear organization in the following interphase.
source: Interestingly, loss of the perichromosomal layer does not detectibly compromise the condensed morphology or intrinsic structure of mitotic chromosomes but does result in significant changes in nucleolar morphology and nuclear organization in the following interphase.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data on nucleolar number, size, and chromosome positioning.

claim: When the nucleolus disassembles during open mitosis, many nucleolar proteins and RNAs associate with chromosomes, establishing a perichromosomal compartment coating the chromosome periphery.
source: When the nucleolus disassembles during open mitosis, many nucleolar proteins and RNAs associate with chromosomes, establishing a perichromosomal compartment coating the chromosome periphery.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about nucleolar disassembly during mitosis.

claim: The perichromosomal layer includes pre-rRNA, U3 snoRNAs, and over 20 ribosomal proteins.
source: This perichromosomal layer includes pre-rRNA, U3 snoRNAs, and over 20 ribosomal proteins, including nucleolin and Nopp140, NPM/B23, Bop1, Nop52, PM-Scl 100, and Ki-67 (Gautier et al., 1992a, 1994; Hernandez-Verdun and Gautier, 1994; Van Hooser et al., 2005; Fomproix et al., 1998; Angelier et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Depletion of nucleolin resulted in the loss of both fibrillarin and nucleophosmin (NPM/B23) from the perichromosomal layer.
source: It had previously been published that depletion of nucleolin resulted in the loss of both fibrillarin and nucleophosmin (NPM/B23) from the perichromosomal layer (Ma et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Nucleolin association with mitotic chromosomes depends on Ki-67.
source: Our studies reveal that nucleolin association with mitotic chromosomes depends on Ki-67, and therefore begin to define a pathway for assembly of the perichromosomal compartment.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing nucleolin mislocalization after Ki-67 depletion.

claim: Casein kinase II phosphorylation of B23 at S125 is important for regulating its dynamics and molecular chaperone activity.
source: Casein kinase II phosphorylation of B23 at S125 is important for regulating its dynamics and molecular chaperone activity (Szebeni et al., 2003; Negi and Olson, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ki-67 has been reported to bind DNA.
source: Ki-67 has been reported to bind DNA (MacCallum and Hall, 2000a) and to interact with HP1 family members (Kametaka et al., 2002; Scholzen et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Ki-67 has been reported to interact with HP1 family members.
source: Ki-67 has been reported to bind DNA (MacCallum and Hall, 2000a) and to interact with HP1 family members (Kametaka et al., 2002; Scholzen et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: After 48 hr of Ki-67 depletion, the mitotic chromosomes appear to be no more susceptible to DNA damage than normal.
source: After 48 hr of Ki-67 depletion, the mitotic chromosomes appear to be no more susceptible to DNA damage than normal, have a normal morphology in cytogenetic spreads, and behave normally in our intrinsic metaphase structure assay, which can detect defects in chromosome architecture that are not readily apparent by simple examination of the chromosomes (Hudson et al., 2003; Samejima et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from DNA damage assays.

claim: After 48 hr of Ki-67 depletion, mitotic chromosomes have a normal morphology in cytogenetic spreads.
source: After 48 hr of Ki-67 depletion, the mitotic chromosomes appear to be no more susceptible to DNA damage than normal, have a normal morphology in cytogenetic spreads, and behave normally in our intrinsic metaphase structure assay, which can detect defects in chromosome architecture that are not readily apparent by simple examination of the chromosomes (Hudson et al., 2003; Samejima et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from chromosome spreads.

claim: After 48 hr of Ki-67 depletion, mitotic chromosomes behave normally in the intrinsic metaphase structure assay.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from IMS assays.

claim: Nuclei that reassemble following Ki-67 depletion are smaller than control nuclei.
source: Importantly, nuclei that reassemble following Ki-67 depletion are smaller than control nuclei, the location of at least one chromosomal locus within the nucleus is altered and they possess a single large nucleolus.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative microscopy data.

claim: The loss of Ki-67 and the perichromosomal layer allows acrocentric chromosomes to cluster during nuclear reformation with resultant formation of a single nucleolus as a result of fusion of several nucleolus organizing regions (NORs).
source: All of these observations can be explained by two effects of Ki-67 depletion. First, the loss of Ki-67 and the perichromosomal layer apparently allows acrocentric chromosomes to cluster during nuclear reformation with resultant formation of a single nucleolus as a result of fusion of several nucleolus organizing regions (NORs).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation of reduced nucleolar number after Ki-67 depletion.

claim: The loss of Ki-67 and the perichromosomal compartment causes a decrease in the efficiency of NOR reactivation during mitotic exit.
source: Second, the loss of Ki-67 and the perichromosomal compartment also causes a decrease in the efficiency of NOR reactivation during mitotic exit.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple observations including nucleolar area, rRNA levels, and chromosome positioning.

claim: Mutations in the TOR pathway tend to give rise to smaller cells.
source: For example, mutations in the TOR pathway, an important regulator of protein translation, tend to give rise to smaller cells (Miron and Sonenberg, 2001; Jewell and Guan, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: All nucleolar components examined ultimately find their way back into nucleoli during interphase following Ki-67 RNAi, despite exhibiting a highly abnormal distribution in mitotic cells.
source: Although the nucleolar components we examined exhibit a highly abnormal distribution in mitotic cells following Ki-67 RNAi, all of them ultimately find their way back into nucleoli during the subsequent interphase.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy observations.

claim: The pathway of nucleolar reassembly exhibits a remarkable degree of plasticity.
source: Thus, the pathway of nucleolar reassembly exhibits a remarkable degree of plasticity.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that nucleoli reform despite abnormal protein distribution during mitosis.

claim: The segregation of at least one major nucleolar component is noticeably more variable following Ki-67 depletion.
source: Furthermore, the segregation of at least one major nucleolar component is noticeably more variable following Ki-67 depletion, suggesting that association with the chromosomes may contribute to the accurate and efficient segregation of the ribosome synthesis machinery at cell division.

claim: During nuclear envelope reassembly, vesicle association and fusion on the chromosomal surface to make the double membrane bilayer precede the assembly of functional nuclear pores.
source: During nuclear envelope reassembly, vesicle association and fusion on the chromosomal surface to make the double membrane bilayer precede the assembly of functional nuclear pores (Kutay and Hetzer, 2008).

claim: During mitotic exit, there is a brief period during which the chromatin is insulated from contact with the cytoplasm.
source: Thus, during mitotic exit, there is a brief period during which the chromatin is insulated from contact with the cytoplasm (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from knowledge about nuclear envelope reassembly.

claim: The ribosomal components of the perichromosomal compartment are inside the membrane barrier when it forms during mitotic exit.
source: Their association with the chromosomal surface as the nuclear envelope is laid down at the end of mitosis, means that the ribosomal components of the perichromosomal compartment are inside the membrane barrier when it forms.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the localization of perichromosomal proteins and the process of nuclear envelope reassembly.

claim: Early access to NOR chromatin and the high protein concentration within small decondensing G1 nuclei may be critical factors in NOR reactivation, thereby 'jump starting' nucleolar reassembly.

source: Indeed, it has previously been shown that assembly of prenucleolar bodies, an early step in nucleolar reassembly takes place on the chromosome periphery (Savino et al., 2001).

claim: In the absence of Ki-67 and of the chromosomal periphery there will be a period of time during mitotic exit when nucleolar components in the cytoplasm are denied access to the chromosomes.

evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental observations and knowledge of nuclear envelope reassembly.

claim: Ki-67-depleted cells appear to survive with their single nucleolus and can proceed to another cell cycle.
source: Remarkably, although the abnormalities in the dispersal and re-aggregation of nucleolar components during mitosis appear quite dramatic, Ki-67-depleted cells appear to survive with their single nucleolus and can proceed to another cell cycle.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: An increase of apoptosis together with mitotic delay was observed at the second division after Ki-67 depletion.
source: This second division becomes more problematic and we have observed an increase of apoptosis together with mitotic delay.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: Ki-67 functions as a structural/scaffolding protein required for assembly of the perichromosomal compartment on condensed mitotic chromosomes.
source: Our studies have revealed for the first time that Ki-67 functions as a structural/scaffolding protein required for assembly of the perichromosomal compartment on condensed mitotic chromosomes.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing that Ki-67 is required for localization of multiple perichromosomal proteins and that PP1-binding is not required for this function.

claim: Ki-67 has an important role in determining the behaviour of many nucleolar components during mitosis.
source: Thus, Ki-67 has an important role in determining the behaviour of many nucleolar components during mitosis.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing mislocalization of multiple nucleolar proteins after Ki-67 depletion.

claim: The method of segregating nucleolar components via the perichromosomal layer means that nucleolar reassembly can begin immediately after CDK activity declines and before the re-establishment of nuclear-cytoplasmic transport during mitotic exit.
source: Interestingly, this method of segregating nucleolar components means that nucleolar reassembly can begin immediately after CDK activity declines and before the re-establishment of nuclear-cytoplasmic transport during mitotic exit.
